automate_scope.note: Which Automate tasks are required for the first release has not been decided. Automate tasks are tracked but are neither assumed mandatory nor assumed deferred until a person records that decision here.

invoice-processor.note_python: Verification interpreter. uv otherwise picks the newest installed CPython, and a verdict must be comparable across revisions; the app declares >=3.13 and 3.13 is what its development and the earlier verified runs used.

ew.pytest.unit.note: Whole non-integration suite. Exercises adapters, notifications, scheduling, Connect consumer, queue.

ew.ci.windows_package.note: Builds the NSIS installer, verifies engine process-tree lifecycle, re-runs the packaged engine smoke. A build artifact, not a release.

ds.ci.rust.note: fmt, test all targets/features, clippy on ubuntu-24.04.

ds.cargo.lib.note: Needs frontend build first; ~10 min cold. Opt in with --heavy.

ip.pytest.all.note: Whole suite. tests/test_shell.py shells out to a node static check and needs desktop/node_modules.

xapp.accept_ew_to_ip.note: The acceptance script drives exact extracted Email Watcher and Invoice Processor trees over loopback, with the exact contracts keyring and a stand-in model. All three revisions are recorded. No GPU.

manual.ip_removal_test.note: scripts/removal_test.py: install the .deb, drive the packaged Email Watcher through not-installed / installed / removed. Needs sudo dpkg; a person runs it and records the transcript.

manual.ew_linux_install.note: Install the current Email Watcher Linux artifact on Linux and record the installed-app smoke transcript.

manual.ip_windows_install.note: Install the current Invoice Processor Windows artifact on Windows and record the installed-app smoke transcript.

manual.ds_linux_install.note: Install the current Document Summarizer Linux artifact on Linux and record the installed-app smoke transcript.

manual.ds_windows_install.note: Install the current Document Summarizer Windows artifact on Windows and record the installed-app smoke transcript.

manual.ew_live_calendar.note: Live Microsoft consent, proposal and confirmed write against a real tenant. Recorded in docs/CONTRACTS.md acceptance appendix.

inspect.ew_automation_rules.note: Exact-revision discovery hints only. Marker presence or absence never proves that a user-definable rule exists.

inspect.ew_queue_scheduler.note: Exact-revision discovery hints only. Behavioral evidence is still required.

tasks.title: I hear about the mail that matters, without checking
tasks.promise: Watch chosen senders on Gmail, Microsoft 365, or any IMAP mailbox; read each new message with a local model; tell me what it is, how urgent, and what it asks; notify me on the desktop and optionally my phone.
tasks.human_involvement: You pick the senders and connect the mailbox once. Phone alerts are off until you set a topic.

conditions.proves: All three mail adapters connect and behave read-only in tests.
Desktop and ntfy channels deliver independently; ntfy only with a topic.
Whole suite green on a GitHub Linux runner.
Locking, config and Windows Connect placement tests pass on a Windows runner.

tasks.title: A meeting request in my mail becomes a calendar event I approve
tasks.promise: Without a click, spot a meeting request in watched mail, extract only times traceable to exact quotes, check my calendar, propose a slot, and — only after I confirm one specific proposal — create the event, telling me first who will receive invitations.
tasks.human_involvement: Confirmation is required before anything is written. The automation stops on ambiguous mail and waits for review. Microsoft 365 only.

conditions.proves: Extracted times must trace to source quotes; unsupported dates/zones are dropped.
Runs only with both licence features; reaches a durable confirmation preview; reviewable when no common time.
Event creation is idempotent per transaction and classifies ambiguous outcomes.
A person observed consent, proposal and a confirmed write against a real tenant.

tasks.title: A PDF becomes a summary I can check against the page
tasks.promise: Summarize a text PDF in General, Story or Contract mode; every claim cites an exact source quote and is marked supported, unsupported or ambiguous; warn me when coverage falls short; never modify the file.
tasks.human_involvement: Choose the PDF. Read the warnings. The app suggests a mode; you can override it.

conditions.proves: All targets and features tested, fmt and clippy clean, on a GitHub Linux runner.
Library tests pass on this machine at the exact revision (heavy; opt-in).

tasks.title: A vendor bill is read into a ledger I can audit
tasks.promise: Extract vendor, number, dates, line items and totals with every value tied to a span on the page; withhold what cannot be verified; catch duplicates; track received → reviewed → paid; keep records across uninstall.
tasks.human_involvement: You review each entry before it can be paid. Unresolved duplicates block review.

conditions.proves: The whole Invoice Processor test suite passes at the current revision.
Unknown spans, non-verbatim values and unknown currency are withheld, never guessed.
State machine, duplicate derivation and resolution, purge boundaries.
Uninstall touches nothing under the data directory; nothing claims a signature.

tasks.title: One click summarizes the PDF in my mail
tasks.promise: With both apps installed and licensed, a Summarize action appears on a PDF attachment inside Email Watcher; the file alone is handed over loopback; the cited summary comes back and stays with the message.
tasks.human_involvement: You click. Requires the licence in both apps.

conditions.proves: Summarize handoff persists results, survives provider failure, never masquerades failure as success.
Consumer suite green on GitHub.

tasks.title: An emailed bill appears in my ledger
tasks.promise: With both apps installed and licensed, a Read invoice action appears on a bill inside Email Watcher; the bill is handed to Invoice Processor over loopback; it lands in the ledger through the same path as a hand-opened file, entry marked received, waiting for review.
tasks.human_involvement: You click, and you review the entry before it can be paid. A second bill may wait durably while the provider is busy.

conditions.proves: A Connect job produces a real ledger entry through Ledger.ingest with duplicate detection; the provider writes no ledger table itself.
Generic invoke requires explicit provider and confirmation, persists first, reconciles lost acks.
Exact extracted Email Watcher and Invoice Processor code runs end to end over loopback with the exact contracts keyring, a stand-in model, and all three revisions recorded.
A PROVIDER_BUSY job is held durably and resubmitted with the same identity when pumped.
Packaged apps discover each other, and removal leaves the ledger and the other app untouched.

tasks.title: A PDF from a vendor is summarized before I open it
tasks.promise: A rule I define — this sender, any PDF — hands the file to Document Summarizer without a click and notifies me with the summary in hand.
tasks.human_involvement: You define the rule once; afterward no click is part of the promised flow.

conditions.proves: A person can define a sender-and-attachment rule for this flow.

tasks.title: Bills file themselves and I get a digest
tasks.promise: A rule — this vendor, a PDF that looks like a bill — routes each arrival into the ledger without a click, batches survive a busy provider, and a scheduled digest tells me what arrived and what is due.
tasks.human_involvement: You define the routing and digest rule; review before payment stays with you.

conditions.proves: A person can define a vendor-and-invoice rule for this flow.
The desktop schedules Connect queue pumping without a manual click.

tasks.title: Before we ship: install, licence, model, records, both platforms
tasks.promise: Installers for Linux and Windows for all three apps; first run says whether a model is visible; the licence activates locally; records survive uninstall; published downloads with checksums.
tasks.human_involvement: Signing is a deliberate operator decision, deferred until all three apps and the Connect/Automate flow are proven.
